canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the prevailing usage is image-to-text generation: a model produces a textual description of an input image. Most formulations treat success as accurately describing visible content, often including objects, attributes, spatial relations, or broader scene content, and some prompts explicitly ask for objective descriptions that avoid subjective conjecture. Papers differ mainly in granularity, ranging from brief or single-sentence captions to rich, highly detailed descriptions, and a smaller line of work asks for structured scene descriptions in JSON, style-sensitive captions, or descriptions detailed enough to replace a diagram in downstream problem solving.

Variants. Papers use several near-synonymous labels, including image description, image description generation, visual captioning, scene description, and caption generation. Variants span literal description writing for two-panel comics, diagram and math captioning, medical and pathology images, earth-observation images, situated captioning from an agent's viewpoint, driving-scene description, and open-ended generation. Some studies caption whole images, while others target regions, detected objects, people, or UI observations, or use captions as inputs for later reasoning or summarization.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers link image captioning to 10 measurement instruments. The most common are MS-COCO, Flickr30k, CHAIR, NoCaps, and COCO Caption; benchmark datasets dominate, while CHAIR is used to assess object hallucination in generated captions. The remaining five instruments are less common and include judge-based and human evaluation, with some papers scoring accuracy and detailedness on a Likert scale or testing low-level visual description.

What it is taken as evidence of. Papers link image captioning to 7 constructs, and they use it in several construct-level roles rather than linking it to a single construct. The most common framing connects it to visual understanding, multimodal understanding, visual perception, brain alignment, and generalization: multimodal understanding, visual perception, and generalization are measured by image captioning, image captioning is related to visual understanding, multimodal understanding, and visual perception, and some papers claim a causal relationship from image captioning to visual understanding and brain alignment. Two other constructs are also linked as additional causal targets.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the prevailing usage is image-to-text generation: a model produces a textual description of an input image. Most formulations treat success as accurately describing visible content, often including objects, attributes, spatial relations, or broader scene content, and some prompts explicitly ask for objective descriptions that avoid subjective conjecture. Papers differ mainly in granularity, ranging from brief or single-sentence captions to rich, highly detailed descriptions, and a smaller line of work asks for structured scene descriptions in JSON, style-sensitive captions, or descriptions detailed enough to replace a diagram in downstream problem solving.

characterization_sections.label: Variants.
characterization_sections.text: Papers use several near-synonymous labels, including image description, image description generation, visual captioning, scene description, and caption generation. Variants span literal description writing for two-panel comics, diagram and math captioning, medical and pathology images, earth-observation images, situated captioning from an agent's viewpoint, driving-scene description, and open-ended generation. Some studies caption whole images, while others target regions, detected objects, people, or UI observations, or use captions as inputs for later reasoning or summarization.

characterization_sections.label: Space of elicitation and scores.
characterization_sections.text: Papers link image captioning to 10 measurement instruments. The most common are MS-COCO, Flickr30k, CHAIR, NoCaps, and COCO Caption; benchmark datasets dominate, while CHAIR is used to assess object hallucination in generated captions. The remaining five instruments are less common and include judge-based and human evaluation, with some papers scoring accuracy and detailedness on a Likert scale or testing low-level visual description.

characterization_sections.label: What it is taken as evidence of.
characterization_sections.text: Papers link image captioning to 7 constructs, and they use it in several construct-level roles rather than linking it to a single construct. The most common framing connects it to visual understanding, multimodal understanding, visual perception, brain alignment, and generalization: multimodal understanding, visual perception, and generalization are measured by image captioning, image captioning is related to visual understanding, multimodal understanding, and visual perception, and some papers claim a causal relationship from image captioning to visual understanding and brain alignment. Two other constructs are also linked as additional causal targets.
